correctness.rationale: The domain is exactly 105 labelled unrooted fully binary six-leaf trees and 45 yes/no resolved quartet indicators. Leaf insertion is bijective by deleting the last leaf; an independent compatible-split construction gives identical 105 sorted 45-bit rows (SHA-256 77b2724baaf35916196e7a8a2ec528d9b5b11de538573cb959c638629d7f8cd4). Each four-set has exactly one positive resolution; its 15 independent partition relations give degree-one rank at most 31. The embedded 31-by-31 integer minor has residue 243 modulo 1000003, proving rank at least 31. The 105-by-105 integer degree-two minor has residue 582830 modulo 1000003, proving full rank 105. A separately implemented split checker obtains the same ranks modulo 1000033. The four specified split systems give a verified first-order trade and a pairwise probability gap 1/2. Both actual embedded programs were executed successfully; no extrapolation to other leaf sizes or independent audit is asserted.

value.rationale: The natural 105-state family is the first six-taxon topology class containing both unrooted binary tree shapes, and quartet splits are its standard local observables. Recoverability of arbitrary topology distributions—not mere classification of one tree—is a motivated identifiability problem. The theorem exactly identifies the whole 74-dimensional first-order blind space, proves that one additional joint-observation degree removes every ambiguity, and supplies two concrete indistinguishable mixtures separated by a precise pair event. The finite-domain claim is mathematically meaningful without claiming a general-n formula or noisy stability. The certificate and reproducibility support, but do not themselves constitute, the value argument.
